goal: Let the user take the one main action of a page, card or dialog
how: One filled button per region, in the tone of what it does: brand when it is neutral, go when it sends something outward. Every other action in the region is soft or ghost, and in an end-aligned row the primary comes last.
avoid: Two filled buttons in one row, or a filled delete beside the primary: the destructive action takes the soft or ghost variant on the far side.

goal: Let the user act with a button that shows only an icon
how: .btn--icon makes the box square around one glyph, an aria-label names the button, and a data-tip says what it does where the icon alone does not. In a dense row of secondary actions it is .btn--ghost as well.
avoid: Leaving .btn--icon off, which keeps the text padding and puts the glyph in a box half again as wide as it is tall.

goal: Let the user see that the action they pressed is still running
how: aria-busy="true" on the button while the call is in flight: the label is painted out but keeps its width, a ring spins in its place, and a second click is ignored. The handler ignores a second Enter until the work is done.
avoid: Setting disabled while it runs, which drops focus and stops the state being announced.

goal: Let the user find out why an action is unavailable
how: A data-tip on the button says what it is waiting for. Where a keyboard reader needs the reason, aria-disabled="true" keeps the button in the tab order with the same look, and the handler ignores it.
avoid: Hiding the action instead, which leaves the reader looking for something that is not there.

goal: Let the user start the screen's main task from a floating button on a phone
how: One .fab pinned to a corner for the one action a small screen has no toolbar for; .fab--icon is the round form named by its aria-label. A .fab-dial fans three to five related actions out of it as a menu.
avoid: Using a floating button on a screen wide enough for the page head, where the action belongs in .page-head-actions.

goal: Let the user reach a few actions on the same thing as one control
how: .btn-group shares one border between neighbours so the buttons read as one control, and role="group" with an aria-label says what they act on. Every button in it takes the same size class.
avoid: Using a button group to pick one of several options, which is a segmented control and is announced as a choice.

goal: Let the user run an action or pick a variant of it from one control
how: .split-btn is two real buttons: the action, which works without opening anything, and a caret with its own name and aria-expanded that opens a .menu of the variants. A destructive variant goes last in the menu as .menu-item--danger.
avoid: Making the whole control open the menu, so the common case takes two clicks.

goal: Let the user search a list and narrow it with a few controls above it
how: A .toolbar above the list: the search and one or two selects in .toolbar-filters, the count of what is left at the trailing end. A search whose placeholder is a sentence takes .toolbar-input--wide or --grow.
avoid: A third child in the toolbar, which space-between floats into the middle: everything belongs to the filters or the actions.

goal: Let the user act on all the rows they selected at once
how: While rows are selected the toolbar says how many in words, with Select all and Clear on the leading side and the actions on the selection at the trailing end. Anything destructive goes in the overflow menu, naming the count it acts on.
avoid: Treating the rows on one page as the whole result set: selecting all of the results is a separate, explicit choice.

goal: Let the user reach every action when a row of them runs out of room
how: .toolbar-actions--fold hides every child but .actions-more and those marked .actions-keep once the toolbar is narrow, and the menu behind .actions-more holds the same actions. The page head folds the same way by its own width.
avoid: Measuring the row in script to decide what fits: the fold is the container's width, in CSS.

goal: Let the user open a short list of actions from one button
how: A .menu-anchor around the trigger and the panel, data-menu-toggle on the trigger and hidden on the panel: the script opens one at a time, closes it on a click outside or Escape, and moves between items with the arrow keys. .menu-label, .menu-sep and .menu-item--danger last give it its order.
avoid: Adding role="menu", which promises one tab stop and stops a screen reader announcing the links inside as links.

goal: Let the user right-click a record for its actions
how: data-menu-context names a .menu with the popover attribute, which opens where the reader right-clicked, or under the element for the ContextMenu key. A .menu-sub-anchor holds an item and the submenu it opens beside it.
avoid: Putting an action only in the context menu: the same action has to be reachable from a visible control.

goal: Let the user type to find an item in a long menu
how: An input with data-menu-filter at the top of the panel narrows the items as the reader types, hides a label with nothing left under it, and shows the app's .menu-empty row when nothing matches.
avoid: Filtering a menu of values the reader picks from, which is a searchable select.

goal: Let the user change a status or an access level in place from a menu
how: A .value-trigger shows the current value and opens a menu whose options carry an icon or a description; .col-control gives its column a floor. Name each trigger after the record it changes and the value it holds, and mark that option aria-current in its menu, which tints it and draws its tick.
avoid: A value trigger where a plain list of values would do, which is a select.

goal: Let the user open the detail behind a figure, a state or a term
how: A .popover with the popover attribute, opened by a popovertarget button, which also anchors it: the platform gives it the top layer, light dismiss and Escape. Inside, a title and a sentence, .kv rows, or a small table in .popover--flush.
avoid: Putting a list of actions in a popover, which is a menu.

goal: Let the user glance at a record by resting on its link
how: data-popover-hover beside data-popover opens the card after a short rest or on focus and keeps it while the pointer moves onto it; a long press opens it on touch. A list of many triggers renders one card and fills it for the one reached.
avoid: Putting what the reader needs only in a hover card, which a reader who never rests there does not see.

goal: Let the user put the items of a list in their own order
how: data-drag-zone on the list, data-drag-item on each row and data-drag-handle on its grip; Space picks a row up and the arrow keys move it. The script reports the move as sedna-drop and the app moves the row in its own list.
avoid: Leaving out the live region and its sentences, so a keyboard drag happens in silence.

goal: Let the user move cards between the columns of a board
how: A .drag-board of .drag-lane sections whose zones share a data-drag-group, with one sedna-drop handler on the board naming From and To. Each lane writes its .drag-empty once and its count in its head.
avoid: A board with no keyboard route: the arrows across a lane move the card to the next one, and the announcements say where it went.

goal: Let the user rearrange tiles in a grid by dragging
how: .drag-grid with data-drag-axis="grid" counts positions in reading order, so the index is the same whatever the column count, and the arrow keys move a tile across and between rows.
avoid: Storing a tile's position as a column and a row in a .drag-grid, whose column count follows its width: tiles that keep a place of their own are a .panel-grid.

goal: Let the user open a menu or a list upward from a bar pinned to the foot of a pane
how: --panel-placement on the bar, block-start for above or inline-end and inline-start for beside, reaches every panel anchored to a trigger inside it: menus, popovers, combo fields and selects. Each still turns round where its side has no room, and a menu is a sheet on a phone whatever it says.
avoid: Writing position-area for a library panel in the app's own CSS, which loses the flip and the sheet.
